records.source: Καὶ ἐγένετο ὅτε ἐτέλεσεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς διατάσσων τοῖς δώδεκα μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ, μετέβη ἐκεῖθεν τοῦ διδάσκειν καὶ κηρύσσειν ἐν ταῖς πόλεσιν αὐτῶν.
records.gloss: And it happened when finished the Jesus commanding the twelve disciples of him, he moved on from there to teach and to preach in the cities of them.
pieces: When Jesus had finished giving these instructions to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} twelve disciples, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} moved on from there to teach and to proclaim the message in their towns.

L.1: And it happened, when Jesus had finished instructing {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} twelve disciples, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went on from there to teach and to preach in their towns.

R.1: Jesus finished telling {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} twelve followers what to do. Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} left that place and went to teach and preach in the towns of that area.

decisions.choice: when Jesus had finished: the formula that closes the second long speech
decisions.reason: Matthew ends each great speech with these words (7:28; 13:53; 19:1; 26:1). This one closes the instructions of chapter 10.

decisions.choice: their towns: the towns of the Jewish people of the region
decisions.reason: "Their" has no clear antecedent; it most likely means the people of Galilee, as in 4:23 and 9:35 ("their synagogues"). Matthew does not say here that the twelve set out.

decisions.choice: proclaim the message (B); the towns of that area (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced says what was proclaimed; Readable says which towns are meant.

records.source: Ὁ δὲ Ἰωάννης ἀκούσας ἐν τῷ δεσμωτηρίῳ τὰ ἔργα τοῦ χριστοῦ πέμψας διὰ τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Σὺ εἶ ὁ ἐρχόμενος ἢ ἕτερον προσδοκῶμεν;
records.gloss: And John having heard in the prison the works of the Christ, having sent through the disciples of him, \v 3 said to him, You are the coming [one] or another are we to expect?
pieces: Meanwhile John, now in prison, heard about the works of the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}. He sent word by his disciples
and asked {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} the one who is coming, or should we wait for someone else?"

L.2: Now John, having heard in prison about the works of the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, sent [word] through his disciples
L.3: [and] said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} the one who is coming, or are we to look for another?"

R.2: John the Baptist was in prison. He heard about the things the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} was doing. So he sent some of his followers to Jesus.
R.3: They asked {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} the one God promised to send? Or should we wait for someone else?"

decisions.choice: in prison: John had been arrested by Herod Antipas
decisions.reason: Matthew mentions John's arrest in 4:12 and tells its cause in 14:3-5. The Jewish historian Josephus places the prison at the fortress of Machaerus, east of the Dead Sea.

decisions.choice: the works of the Christ: what Jesus had been doing, told in chapters 8-9
alternatives: works John had heard of only by rumor
decisions.reason: Matthew, the narrator, calls them the Messiah's works. John asks whether they mean what he hopes. The same word returns in 11:19 ("her deeds").

decisions.choice: the one who is coming: the one John had announced
decisions.reason: John had said "the one who comes after me" (3:11). The phrase echoes Psalm 118:26 and Malachi 3:1, where the coming one brings God's judgment and salvation.

decisions.choice: through his disciples, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: two of his disciples, the reading of many later manuscripts
decisions.reason: The two Greek words differ by a letter or two; many later manuscripts read "two", perhaps under the influence of Luke 7:18-19. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: the one God promised to send
decisions.reason: Readable says what "the one who is coming" meant to John and his hearers.

records.heading: John's question from prison

records.source: καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Πορευθέντες ἀπαγγείλατε Ἰωάννῃ ἃ ἀκούετε καὶ βλέπετε·
records.gloss: And answering the Jesus said to them, Having gone report to John what you hear and see:
pieces: Jesus answered them, "Go back and tell John what you are hearing and seeing:

L.4: And Jesus answered and said to them, "Go [and] report to John what you hear and see:

R.4: Jesus answered, "Go back and tell John about the things you hear and see.

decisions.choice: what you hear and see: Jesus's words and his deeds
decisions.reason: Matthew has given Jesus's teaching (chapters 5-7) and his works (chapters 8-9). Jesus lets them speak for him instead of answering "yes" directly.

records.source: τυφλοὶ ἀναβλέπουσιν καὶ χωλοὶ περιπατοῦσιν, λεπροὶ καθαρίζονται καὶ κωφοὶ ἀκούουσιν, καὶ νεκροὶ ἐγείρονται καὶ πτωχοὶ εὐαγγελίζονται·
records.gloss: Blind receive sight and lame walk, lepers are cleansed and deaf hear, and dead are raised and poor are told good news;
pieces: the blind can see and the lame are walking, people with leprosy are made clean and the deaf can hear, the dead are raised to life, and the poor are hearing the good news.

L.5: [the] blind receive sight and [the] lame walk, lepers are cleansed and [the] deaf hear, and [the] dead are raised and [the] poor have good news proclaimed [to them].

R.5: Blind people can see again. People who could not walk are walking. People with bad skin diseases are healed. Deaf people can hear. Dead people are brought back to life. And poor people are hearing the good news.

decisions.choice: the signs Isaiah promised for the time when God comes to save
alternatives: a simple report with no background
decisions.reason: Isaiah 35:5-6 promises that the blind will see, the deaf hear and the lame leap; 26:19 that the dead will live; and 61:1 that good news will be brought to the poor. Jesus answers John with Scripture.

decisions.choice: each of these has happened in chapters 8-9
alternatives: only a promise for the future
decisions.reason: Lepers (8:2-3), the lame (9:2-7), the dead (9:18-25), the blind (9:27-30) and one who could not speak (9:32-33).

decisions.choice: deaf: those who cannot hear
decisions.reason: The word can mean either (in 9:32 it means unable to speak). Here it is paired with "hear", as in Isaiah 35:5.

decisions.choice: have good news proclaimed (L); are hearing the good news (B, R)
alternatives: have the gospel preached to them
decisions.reason: The verb is the one Isaiah 61:1 uses in the Greek version. "Good news" keeps that echo and suits every level.

records.source: καὶ μακάριός ἐστιν ὃς ἐὰν μὴ σκανδαλισθῇ ἐν ἐμοί.
records.gloss: And blessed is whoever not is caused to stumble in me.
pieces: And blessed is the one who does not take offense at {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."

L.6: And blessed is whoever does not stumble over {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."

R.6: Blessed is anyone who is not upset by what I do and does not turn away from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."

decisions.choice: stumble over me: be offended by Jesus and so fall away
alternatives: be led into sin by me
decisions.reason: The verb pictures tripping over an obstacle. Jesus was not the kind of Messiah many expected; John himself had spoken of fire and judgment (3:10-12).

decisions.choice: blessed: favored by God, as in 5:3-11
decisions.reason: The same word begins each saying in 5:3-11.

decisions.choice: is not upset by what I do and does not turn away from me
decisions.reason: Readable spells out the picture of stumbling.

records.source: Τούτων δὲ πορευομένων ἤρξατο ὁ Ἰησοῦς λέγειν τοῖς ὄχλοις περὶ Ἰωάννου· Τί ἐξήλθατε εἰς τὴν ἔρημον θεάσασθαι;
records.gloss: These and going began the Jesus to say to the crowds about John, What did you go out into the wilderness to look at?
pieces: While they were on their way, Jesus started speaking to the crowds about John. "When you went out into the wilderness, what did you go to look at?

L.7: And as these were going away, Jesus began to say to the crowds about John, "What did you go out into the wilderness to look at?

R.7: While John's followers were going away, Jesus began to talk to the crowds about John. He asked them, "You went out to the desert. What did you expect to see there?

decisions.choice: the wilderness: where John preached and baptized
decisions.reason: Crowds went out to John in the wilderness of Judea, by the Jordan (3:1-6).

decisions.choice: to look at: to gaze, as at a spectacle
decisions.reason: The verb is used of watching something worth seeing. Jesus asks what drew the crowds.

decisions.choice: John's followers; He asked them
decisions.reason: Readable says who was leaving and that Jesus asked a question.

records.heading: Jesus speaks about John

records.source: κάλαμον ὑπὸ ἀνέμου σαλευόμενον;
records.gloss: A reed by wind being shaken?
pieces: A reed blowing back and forth in the wind?

R.7: A weak reed that bends whichever way the wind blows?

decisions.choice: a reed shaken by the wind: a weak person who gives way to every pressure
alternatives: the plain reeds along the Jordan
decisions.reason: Reeds grew along the Jordan, and the question may begin there, but the picture is of someone easily swayed (1 Kings 14:15). John was not that kind of man.

decisions.choice: a weak reed that bends whichever way the wind blows
alternatives: a reed shaken by the wind
decisions.reason: Readable shows what the picture means.

records.source: ἀλλὰ τί ἐξήλθατε ἰδεῖν;
records.gloss: But what did you go out to see?
pieces: If not, what did you go out to see?

L.8: But what did you go out to see?

R.8: Then what did you go out to see?

decisions.choice: but: the answer to the first question is no
decisions.reason: Each question expects "no", and "but" moves on to the next guess.

records.source: ἄνθρωπον ἐν μαλακοῖς ἠμφιεσμένον;
records.gloss: A man in soft [clothes] having been dressed?
pieces: Someone wearing soft, costly clothing?

R.8: A man wearing fancy, expensive clothes?

decisions.choice: soft clothes: fine, luxurious garments
decisions.reason: Soft cloth was expensive. John wore camel's hair and a leather belt (3:4).

records.source: ἰδοὺ οἱ τὰ μαλακὰ φοροῦντες ἐν τοῖς οἴκοις τῶν βασιλέων εἰσίν.
records.gloss: Behold, those the soft wearing in the houses of the kings are.
pieces: Those who dress in luxury are found in the palaces of kings.

L.8: Look, those who wear soft [clothes] are in the houses of kings.

R.8: No, people who wear clothes like that live in the palaces of kings.

decisions.choice: the houses of kings: royal courts, such as Herod's
decisions.reason: John had denounced Herod Antipas (14:3-4) and was now in his prison, not his court.

decisions.choice: look (L); not rendered (B); no (R)
decisions.reason: As in 1:20, Literal uses "look". Readable carries its force with "no".

records.source: ἀλλὰ τί ἐξήλθατε;
records.gloss: But why did you go out?
pieces: Why did you go out, then?

L.9: But why did you go out?

R.9: So why did you go out there?

decisions.choice: But why did you go out? To see a prophet? Two questions
alternatives: But what did you go out to see? A prophet?
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT ends the question after "go out", so the word can mean "why". With the other punctuation it means "what", as in 11:7-8. The sense is the same.

records.source: προφήτην ἰδεῖν;
records.gloss: A prophet to see?
pieces: To see a prophet?

decisions.choice: a prophet: the people regarded John as a prophet
decisions.reason: The crowds held John to be a prophet (14:5; 21:26).

records.source: ναί, λέγω ὑμῖν, καὶ περισσότερον προφήτου.
records.gloss: Yes, I say to you, and more than a prophet.
pieces: Yes indeed, I tell you, and he is even more than a prophet.

L.9: Yes, I tell you, and more than a prophet.

R.9: Yes, he is a prophet. But I tell you, he is even more than a prophet.

decisions.choice: more than a prophet: John is the messenger the prophets foretold
alternatives: a greater speaker than the prophets
decisions.reason: Other prophets spoke of the coming day; John was himself spoken of, as 11:10 shows.

records.source: οὗτός ἐστιν περὶ οὗ γέγραπται· Ἰδοὺ ἐγὼ ἀποστέλλω τὸν ἄγγελόν μου πρὸ προσώπου σου, ὃς κατασκευάσει τὴν ὁδόν σου ἔμπροσθέν σου.
records.gloss: This is about whom it has been written: Behold, I send the messenger of me before face of you, who will prepare the way of you before you.
pieces: This is the man of whom Scripture says, 'I am sending {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} messenger ahead of {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}; he will make ready {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} way in front of {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.'

L.10: This is [the one] about whom it is written: 'Look, I am sending {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} messenger before {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} face, who will prepare {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} way before {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.'

R.10: John is the one the Scriptures were talking about when God said, 'I will send {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} messenger ahead of {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. He will prepare the way for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.'

decisions.choice: Malachi 3:1, joined with Exodus 23:20
decisions.reason: "I am sending my messenger before your face" matches the Greek of Exodus 23:20, where God sends his angel ahead of Israel. "He will prepare the way" is from Malachi 3:1, where the messenger goes before God himself.

decisions.choice: your: the one for whom the way is prepared is Jesus
decisions.reason: In Malachi the messenger prepares the way "before me", that is, before God. Here God speaks to another, the one who comes, and the coming of God is the coming of Jesus.

decisions.choice: messenger: one sent with a message
decisions.reason: The word can mean either. Here it is John, a human messenger.

decisions.choice: look (L); not rendered (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 1:20, Literal uses "look" and Balanced and Readable carry the word's force in the flow of the sentence.

decisions.choice: when God said
decisions.reason: Readable names the speaker, since "my" and "I" in the quotation are God.

records.source: ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, οὐκ ἐγήγερται ἐν γεννητοῖς γυναικῶν μείζων Ἰωάννου τοῦ βαπτιστοῦ· ὁ δὲ μικρότερος ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ τῶν οὐρανῶν μείζων αὐτοῦ ἐστιν.
records.gloss: Truly I say to you, not has arisen among born of women greater than John the Baptist; the but lesser in the kingdom of the heavens greater than him is.
pieces: Truly I tell you, of all who have ever been born of women, no one has appeared who is greater than John the Baptist. Yet even the smallest in the kingdom of heaven is greater than he is.

L.11: Truly I tell you, among those born of women there has not arisen [anyone] greater than John the Baptist; yet the least in the kingdom of the heavens is greater than he.

R.11: I tell you the truth, no one who has ever lived is greater than John the Baptist. But even the least important person in the kingdom of heaven is greater than John.

decisions.choice: born of women: human beings
decisions.reason: The phrase means all people (Job 14:1).

decisions.choice: the least: the comparative form used as "least"
alternatives: the one who is less (or younger), meaning Jesus
decisions.reason: Greek of this period often uses the comparative for the superlative. Some early readers took "the lesser one" to be Jesus, younger than John, but the contrast is between John and anyone in the kingdom.

decisions.choice: greater: by belonging to the kingdom, not by personal worth
alternatives: John is excluded from the kingdom
decisions.reason: John announced the kingdom and stands at the turn of the ages (11:13). Those who share in it as it comes have a greater privilege than even the greatest prophet.

decisions.choice: I tell you the truth (R); Truly I tell you (L, B)
decisions.reason: As in 5:18, Readable puts Jesus's solemn opening in everyday words.

records.source: ἀπὸ δὲ τῶν ἡμερῶν Ἰωάννου τοῦ βαπτιστοῦ ἕως ἄρτι ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν βιάζεται, καὶ βιασταὶ ἁρπάζουσιν αὐτήν.
records.gloss: From and the days of John the Baptist until now the kingdom of the heavens suffers violence, and violent [ones] seize it.
pieces: From the time of John the Baptist until now, the kingdom of heaven has been suffering violence, and violent people are snatching at it.

L.12: And from the days of John the Baptist until now, the kingdom of the heavens suffers violence, and violent [people] seize it.

R.12: From the time John the Baptist began preaching until now, the kingdom of heaven has been attacked. Violent people are trying to take it by force.

decisions.choice: the kingdom suffers violence, and violent people try to seize it
alternatives: the kingdom is forcefully advancing, and forceful people lay hold of it
the kingdom is entered by force, as Luke 16:16 says everyone forces their way in
decisions.reason: The verb can be passive ("suffers violence") or middle ("advances with force"), and the second clause can be hostile or eager. This verse is among the hardest in Matthew. The noun "violent people" and the verb "seize" are usually negative, and John is in prison, so the hostile reading is taken here.

decisions.choice: from the days of John until now: since John began to preach
decisions.reason: John's ministry marks the start of the new time (11:13). His arrest (4:12; 14:3-10) and the rising opposition to Jesus (9:34; 10:16-25) show the kingdom under attack.

decisions.choice: has been suffering violence (B); has been attacked (R)
decisions.reason: The present tense describes something going on from John's days until now.

decisions.choice: the time John the Baptist began preaching
alternatives: the days of John the Baptist
decisions.reason: Readable says which days are meant.

records.source: πάντες γὰρ οἱ προφῆται καὶ ὁ νόμος ἕως Ἰωάννου ἐπροφήτευσαν·
records.gloss: All for the prophets and the law until John prophesied;
pieces: For all the prophets and the law spoke of what was coming, until John.

L.13: For all the prophets and the law prophesied until John.

R.13: All the prophets and the law of Moses told about what was going to happen, until John came.

decisions.choice: prophesied: pointed ahead to the coming kingdom
decisions.reason: Until John the Scriptures looked forward; with John the time of fulfillment begins. Jesus does not set the law aside (5:17-18).

decisions.choice: the prophets and the law: an unusual order
alternatives: the usual "the law and the prophets"
decisions.reason: Elsewhere Matthew writes "the law and the prophets" (5:17; 7:12). Putting the prophets first stresses that even the law spoke of what was to come.

decisions.choice: the law of Moses
decisions.reason: Readable says which law is meant.

records.source: καὶ εἰ θέλετε δέξασθαι, αὐτός ἐστιν Ἠλίας ὁ μέλλων ἔρχεσθαι.
records.gloss: And if you are willing to receive [it], he is Elijah the one about to come.
pieces: And, if you will receive it, John is Elijah, whose coming was foretold.

L.14: And if you are willing to accept [it], he is Elijah, who is to come.

R.14: If you are willing to accept this, John is the Elijah that God said would come.

decisions.choice: Elijah who is to come: Malachi 4:5
decisions.reason: God promised to send Elijah the prophet before the great day of the LORD (Malachi 4:5; 3:23 in the Hebrew). Jesus says the same in 17:10-13.

decisions.choice: he is Elijah: John fulfills Elijah's role
decisions.reason: In John 1:21 the Baptist denies that he is Elijah himself. He comes "in the spirit and power of Elijah" (Luke 1:17).

decisions.choice: if you are willing to accept it: the claim needs an open heart
decisions.reason: Many expected Elijah himself. Seeing John as the promised Elijah means seeing Jesus as the one who follows.

decisions.choice: John
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name John, since Jesus has just spoken of the law and the prophets.

records.source: ὁ ἔχων ὦτα ἀκουέτω.
records.gloss: The one having ears let him hear.
pieces: Whoever has ears must listen.

L.15: The one who has ears, let him hear.

R.15: If you can hear {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, pay attention to this!

decisions.choice: whoever has ears, let him hear: a call to listen closely and take the saying to heart
decisions.reason: Jesus uses the same words after other sayings that need thought (13:9, 43).

decisions.choice: If you can hear me, pay attention to this!
alternatives: The one who has ears, let him hear
decisions.reason: Readable gives the force of the saying in plain words.

records.source: Τίνι δὲ ὁμοιώσω τὴν γενεὰν ταύτην;
records.gloss: To what but will I compare the generation this?
pieces: What picture shall I use for the people of this generation?

L.16: But to what shall I compare this generation?

R.16: How can I describe the people living today?

decisions.choice: this generation: the people of Jesus's day, taken as a whole
decisions.reason: Jesus uses the phrase of the people who rejected both John and himself (12:39-45; 23:36).

records.heading: Children in the marketplace

records.source: ὁμοία ἐστὶν παιδίοις καθημένοις ἐν ταῖς ἀγοραῖς ἃ προσφωνοῦντα τοῖς ἑτέροις λέγουσιν· Ηὐλήσαμεν ὑμῖν καὶ οὐκ ὠρχήσασθε· ἐθρηνήσαμεν καὶ οὐκ ἐκόψασθε·
records.gloss: Like it is to children sitting in the marketplaces who calling out to the others \v 17 say, We piped for you and not you danced; we lamented and not you beat [your breasts];
pieces: They are like children who sit in the town squares and call out to the other children,
'We played the pipe for you, but you did not dance; we sang a funeral song, but you did not beat your breasts in grief.'

L.16: It is like children sitting in the marketplaces who call out to the others,
L.17: saying, 'We played the flute for you, and you did not dance; we sang a lament, and you did not beat [your breasts].'

R.16: They are like children sitting in the marketplace. They call out to the other children,
R.17: 'We played happy music for you, but you would not dance. We sang sad songs for you, but you would not cry.'

decisions.choice: children's games of wedding and funeral
decisions.reason: Children copied adult life in the public square: the flute and dancing of a wedding, the laments and breast-beating of mourners.

decisions.choice: the children who call out stand for this generation, who wanted John and Jesus to play their tune
alternatives: the calling children are John and Jesus, and this generation would not respond
decisions.reason: "This generation" is like the children who call out. 11:18-19 then shows them finding fault with both John's fasting and Jesus's feasting.

decisions.choice: played happy music; sang sad songs
alternatives: played the flute; sang a lament
decisions.reason: Readable says what kind of music each was.

records.source: ἦλθεν γὰρ Ἰωάννης μήτε ἐσθίων μήτε πίνων, καὶ λέγουσιν· Δαιμόνιον ἔχει·
records.gloss: Came for John neither eating nor drinking, and they say, A demon he has.
pieces: For when John came, he did not eat or drink as others do, and people say, 'There is a demon in him.'

L.18: For John came neither eating nor drinking, and they say, 'He has a demon.'

R.18: John went without food and did not drink wine. And people say, 'A demon has control of him!'

decisions.choice: neither eating nor drinking: John's strict, simple life
alternatives: he ate and drank nothing at all
decisions.reason: John lived on locusts and wild honey (3:4), fasted (9:14), and drank no wine (Luke 1:15).

decisions.choice: he has a demon: he is mad, controlled by an evil spirit
decisions.reason: The charge was a way of dismissing someone as out of his mind (John 10:20).

decisions.choice: as others do (B); went without food and did not drink wine (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable show that ordinary meals and wine are meant.

records.source: ἦλθεν ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐσθίων καὶ πίνων, καὶ λέγουσιν· Ἰδοὺ ἄνθρωπος φάγος καὶ οἰνοπότης, τελωνῶν φίλος καὶ ἁμαρτωλῶν.
records.gloss: Came the Son of the Man eating and drinking, and they say, Behold, a man glutton and drunkard, of tax collectors friend and of sinners.
pieces: The Son of Man came and ate and drank, and they say, 'Look at {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}! He eats too much and drinks too much, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is a friend of tax collectors and sinners!'

L.19: The Son of Man came eating and drinking, and they say, 'Look, a man [who is] a glutton and a drunkard, a friend of tax collectors and sinners!'

R.19: The Son of Man came, eating and drinking with people. And they say, 'Look at {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}! He eats too much and drinks too much wine. He is a friend of tax collectors and sinners!'

decisions.choice: a glutton and a drunkard: the charge against a rebellious son
decisions.reason: The same pair of words describes the rebellious son in Deuteronomy 21:20 (in the Greek version), who was to be put to death.

decisions.choice: friend of tax collectors and sinners: Jesus ate with them
decisions.reason: See 9:10-11. Eating together was a sign of acceptance.

decisions.choice: the Son of Man: Jesus speaking of himself
decisions.reason: Jesus's way of speaking of himself (8:20; 9:6).

decisions.choice: look (L); look at him (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 1:20, Literal uses "look" and Balanced and Readable carry the word's force in the flow of the sentence.

decisions.choice: he is (B)
decisions.reason: "A man" is the speakers' scornful way of pointing at Jesus. Balanced says "he". Inside the speakers' words the pronoun still refers to Jesus, so it takes the deity_pronoun setting except at the start of a sentence.

records.source: καὶ ἐδικαιώθη ἡ σοφία ἀπὸ τῶν ἔργων αὐτῆς.
records.gloss: And was justified the wisdom by the works of her.
pieces: Yet the deeds of wisdom show that she is in the right."

L.19: And wisdom was vindicated by her deeds."

R.19: But what wisdom does shows that wisdom is right."

decisions.choice: her deeds, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: her children, the reading of many manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts read "children", as Luke 7:35 does. The earliest witnesses of Matthew are thought to read "deeds", and copyists probably brought Matthew into line with Luke. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: wisdom: God's wise purpose, seen in the ways of John and of Jesus
decisions.reason: Wisdom is pictured as a woman, as in Proverbs 8-9. Her deeds are the works of the Messiah (11:2), the same word in Greek, which frames this section.

decisions.choice: was vindicated: a past tense stating a general truth
decisions.reason: The past tense here states what always proves to be so; Balanced and Readable use the present.

decisions.choice: vindicated (L); show that she is in the right (B); shows that wisdom is right (R)
decisions.reason: The verb means shown to be in the right. "Justified" would suggest being forgiven.

records.source: Τότε ἤρξατο ὀνειδίζειν τὰς πόλεις ἐν αἷς ἐγένοντο αἱ πλεῖσται δυνάμεις αὐτοῦ, ὅτι οὐ μετενόησαν·
records.gloss: Then he began to reproach the cities in which happened the most miracles of him, because not they repented:
pieces: Then Jesus began to reproach the towns that had seen most of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mighty works, for they had not repented.

L.20: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} began to reproach the towns in which most of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mighty works had happened, because they did not repent:

R.20: Then Jesus began to speak strongly against the towns where {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had done most of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} miracles. The people there had not turned away from their sins and come back to God.

decisions.choice: mighty works: acts of power, miracles
decisions.reason: The plural of the word for power means deeds that show God's power.

decisions.choice: repent: turn from sin back to God
decisions.reason: See the notes on 3:2 and 4:17. The miracles called for a changed life.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Jesus at the start of a new section.

records.heading: Woe to the towns that did not repent

records.source: Οὐαί σοι, Χοραζίν· οὐαί σοι, Βηθσαϊδά· ὅτι εἰ ἐν Τύρῳ καὶ Σιδῶνι ἐγένοντο αἱ δυνάμεις αἱ γενόμεναι ἐν ὑμῖν, πάλαι ἂν ἐν σάκκῳ καὶ σποδῷ μετενόησαν.
records.gloss: Woe to you, Chorazin; woe to you, Bethsaida; for if in Tyre and Sidon had happened the miracles having happened in you, long ago then in sackcloth and ashes they would have repented.
pieces: "Woe to you, Chorazin! Woe to you, Bethsaida! Had Tyre and Sidon seen the mighty works done among you, they would have turned from their sins long ago, dressed in sackcloth and sitting in ashes.

L.21: "Woe to you, Chorazin! Woe to you, Bethsaida! For if in Tyre and Sidon had happened the mighty works that happened in you, long ago they would have repented in sackcloth and ashes.

R.21: "How terrible it will be for you, Chorazin! How terrible for you, Bethsaida! I did many miracles in your towns. If I had done them in Tyre and Sidon, the people there would have turned from their sins long ago. They would have put on rough clothes and sat in ashes to show how sorry they were.

decisions.choice: Chorazin and Bethsaida: Jewish towns near Capernaum at the north end of the Sea of Galilee
decisions.reason: Matthew records none of the miracles done there, but Jesus says they were many.

decisions.choice: Tyre and Sidon: Gentile cities on the coast, condemned by the prophets
decisions.reason: The prophets spoke against them for their pride (Isaiah 23; Ezekiel 26-28). Jesus says they would have done better than the towns of Galilee.

decisions.choice: sackcloth and ashes: signs of grief and repentance
decisions.reason: People wore rough goat-hair cloth and sat in ashes to show sorrow for sin (Jonah 3:6; Daniel 9:3).

decisions.choice: woe: a cry of grief and warning
decisions.reason: The prophets used the word to lament those facing God's judgment (Isaiah 5:8-22).

decisions.choice: How terrible it will be for you (R); Woe to you (L, B)
decisions.reason: Readable explains the old word "woe".

records.source: πλὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, Τύρῳ καὶ Σιδῶνι ἀνεκτότερον ἔσται ἐν ἡμέρᾳ κρίσεως ἢ ὑμῖν.
records.gloss: But I say to you, for Tyre and Sidon more tolerable will it be in day of judgment than for you.
pieces: But I tell you this: on the day of judgment Tyre and Sidon will be better off than you.

L.22: But I tell you, for Tyre and Sidon it will be more bearable on [the] day of judgment than for you.

R.22: But I tell you, on the day God judges all people, it will be easier for Tyre and Sidon than for you.

decisions.choice: more bearable on the day of judgment: judgment will match what each place was given
alternatives: all who reject God are judged alike
decisions.reason: Jesus says the same of Sodom and Gomorrah in 10:15. Those who saw his works and still refused are more to blame than those who never saw them.

decisions.choice: but: more than that, I tell you
decisions.reason: The word adds a stronger statement.

decisions.choice: the day God judges all people
decisions.reason: Readable says whose judgment is meant.

records.source: καὶ σύ, Καφαρναούμ, μὴ ἕως οὐρανοῦ ὑψωθήσῃ;
records.gloss: And you, Capernaum, not to heaven will you be lifted up?
pieces: And you, Capernaum, will you be exalted as high as heaven?

L.23: And you, Capernaum, will you be lifted up to heaven?

R.23: And you, Capernaum! Do you think you will be lifted up to heaven?

decisions.choice: lifted to heaven, brought down to Hades: Isaiah 14:13-15
decisions.reason: Isaiah mocks the king of Babylon, who said, "I will ascend to heaven," but is brought down to the place of the dead. Capernaum's honor of having Jesus live there (4:13) will not save it.

decisions.choice: the question expects the answer "no"
decisions.reason: The negative at the start shows the answer, which the next sentence gives.

decisions.choice: will you be lifted up to heaven?, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: you who have been lifted up to heaven, the reading of many manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts make this a statement about Capernaum's present honor. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

records.source: ἕως ᾅδου καταβήσῃ· ὅτι εἰ ἐν Σοδόμοις ἐγενήθησαν αἱ δυνάμεις αἱ γενόμεναι ἐν σοί, ἔμεινεν ἂν μέχρι τῆς σήμερον.
records.gloss: To Hades you will go down; for if in Sodom had happened the miracles having happened in you, it would have remained until the today.
pieces: No, you will go down to the realm of the dead. If Sodom had seen the mighty works done in you, it would still be standing today.

L.23: You will go down to Hades. For if in Sodom had happened the mighty works that happened in you, it would have remained until today.

R.23: No, you will go down to the place of the dead. If I had done in Sodom the miracles I did in you, Sodom would still be here today.

decisions.choice: Hades: the place of the dead, the lowest place, opposite heaven
alternatives: hell, the place of final punishment
decisions.reason: Hades is the Greek name used for Sheol, the world of the dead. Here it stands for the deepest humiliation, as in Isaiah 14:15. It is a different word from Gehenna (5:22).

decisions.choice: Sodom: the city God destroyed for its wickedness
decisions.reason: See Genesis 19. Sodom was the byword for a city ripe for judgment (10:15).

decisions.choice: you will go down, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: you will be brought down, the reading of many manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts have a passive verb, as in Isaiah 14:15. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: the realm of the dead (B); the place of the dead (R); Hades (L)
decisions.reason: "Hades" is a Greek name that many readers do not know, and "hell" would confuse it with Gehenna. Balanced and Readable say what it is.

decisions.choice: No
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable answer the question of 11:23a.

records.source: πλὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι γῇ Σοδόμων ἀνεκτότερον ἔσται ἐν ἡμέρᾳ κρίσεως ἢ σοί.
records.gloss: But I say to you that for land of Sodom more tolerable will it be in day of judgment than for you.
pieces: But I tell you this: on the day of judgment the land of Sodom will be better off than you."

L.24: But I tell you that for [the] land of Sodom it will be more bearable on [the] day of judgment than for you."

R.24: But I tell you, on the day God judges all people, it will be easier for the land of Sodom than for you."

decisions.choice: more bearable on the day of judgment: judgment will match what each place was given
alternatives: all who reject God are judged alike
decisions.reason: Jesus says the same of Sodom and Gomorrah in 10:15. Those who saw his works and still refused are more to blame than those who never saw them.

decisions.choice: I tell you (plural) ... than for you (singular)
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks to his hearers about Capernaum, then turns back to address the town itself.

decisions.choice: the land of Sodom: Sodom and the towns of its plain
decisions.reason: Genesis 19:25 tells of the overthrow of the cities and the whole plain.

records.source: Ἐν ἐκείνῳ τῷ καιρῷ ἀποκριθεὶς ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν· Ἐξομολογοῦμαί σοι, πάτερ κύριε τοῦ οὐρανοῦ καὶ τῆς γῆς, ὅτι ἔκρυψας ταῦτα ἀπὸ σοφῶν καὶ συνετῶν, καὶ ἀπεκάλυψας αὐτὰ νηπίοις·
records.gloss: At that the time answering the Jesus said, I praise you, Father, Lord of the heaven and the earth, that you hid these from wise and understanding and revealed them to infants;
pieces: At that time Jesus said, "Father, Lord of heaven and earth, I give {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} praise, because {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have kept these things hidden from the wise and the knowledgeable and have made them known to little children.

L.25: At that time Jesus responded and said, "I praise {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, because {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} hid these things from [the] wise and understanding and revealed them to little children.

R.25: Then Jesus prayed, "Father, Lord of heaven and earth, I praise {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}! You have hidden these things from people who are wise and well educated. But {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have shown them to people who are like little children.

decisions.choice: I praise you: I openly give you thanks and acknowledge what you have done
alternatives: I confess my sins to you
decisions.reason: The verb means to declare openly. Addressed to God it is praise and thanks.

decisions.choice: these things: who Jesus is and what his works mean
decisions.reason: The towns saw the works and did not understand (11:20-24); the disciples have begun to see.

decisions.choice: little children: the simple and unlearned, such as the disciples
decisions.reason: The word means infants and so people without learning or standing. Compare 18:3 and 21:16.

decisions.choice: answering: responding to the situation, not to a question
decisions.reason: The word often introduces speech without a question before it.

decisions.choice: Jesus prayed
decisions.reason: Readable says that Jesus is speaking to God. The pronouns "you" for the Father take the deity_pronoun setting, except at the start of a sentence.

records.heading: Hidden from the wise, shown to little children

records.source: ναί, ὁ πατήρ, ὅτι οὕτως εὐδοκία ἐγένετο ἔμπροσθέν σου.
records.gloss: Yes, the Father, for thus good pleasure it was before you.
pieces: Yes, Father, it pleased {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} to have it so.

L.26: Yes, Father, for so it was well-pleasing before {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

R.26: Yes, Father, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} did this because it was what {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} wanted.

decisions.choice: good pleasure: God's gracious choice
decisions.reason: The word is related to the verb in 3:17 ("in whom I am well pleased"). God chose freely to work this way.

decisions.choice: the Father: a form with the article, used as an address
decisions.reason: Greek of this period can use the form with the article to address someone.

records.source: Πάντα μοι παρεδόθη ὑπὸ τοῦ πατρός μου, καὶ οὐδεὶς ἐπιγινώσκει τὸν υἱὸν εἰ μὴ ὁ πατήρ, οὐδὲ τὸν πατέρα τις ἐπιγινώσκει εἰ μὴ ὁ υἱὸς καὶ ᾧ ἐὰν βούληται ὁ υἱὸς ἀποκαλύψαι.
records.gloss: All things to me were handed over by the Father of me, and no one knows the Son except the Father, nor the Father anyone knows except the Son and to whom if wills the Son to reveal.
pieces: My Father has entrusted everything to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. No one fully knows the Son except the Father, and no one fully knows the Father except the Son and those to whom the Son decides to make {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} known.

L.27: All things have been handed over to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} by {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Father, and no one knows the Son except the Father, nor does anyone know the Father except the Son and [anyone] to whom the Son wills to reveal [{{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}].

R.27: My Father has given everything to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. No one really knows the Son except the Father. And no one really knows the Father except the Son. The Son also shows the Father to the people {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} chooses.

decisions.choice: all things have been handed over: the Father has given the Son all authority, including the knowledge of God
alternatives: only the teaching passed on to him
decisions.reason: The verb is used of handing on what one holds. Compare 28:18, "all authority ... has been given to me."

decisions.choice: knows: knows fully and personally
decisions.reason: The verb has a strengthening prefix. The knowing is the close knowledge of a father and son.

decisions.choice: the Son: Jesus speaks of himself as the Son of the Father
decisions.reason: God called Jesus "my Son" at his baptism (3:17). Only the Son can make the Father known, as John 1:18 also says.

decisions.choice: fully knows (B); really knows (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable show the force of the verb.

records.source: Δεῦτε πρός με πάντες οἱ κοπιῶντες καὶ πεφορτισμένοι, κἀγὼ ἀναπαύσω ὑμᾶς.
records.gloss: Come to me all the toiling and having been burdened, and I will give rest you.
pieces: Come to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, all of you who are worn out with work and weighed down with burdens, and I will give you rest.

L.28: Come to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, all who toil and are burdened, and I will give you rest.

R.28: Come to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, all of you who are tired from hard work and from carrying heavy loads. I will give you rest.

decisions.choice: toil: work until worn out
decisions.reason: The verb means to labor hard and grow weary.

decisions.choice: burdened: loaded down, including with the many rules laid on people by their teachers
decisions.reason: The same picture returns in 23:4, where the scribes and Pharisees tie heavy loads on people's shoulders. The invitation is open to all who are weighed down.

decisions.choice: come to me: wisdom's invitation
decisions.reason: In Sirach 51:23-27, a Jewish wisdom book written about two centuries earlier, the teacher calls the untaught to come, take wisdom's yoke on their necks, and find rest. Jesus speaks as wisdom herself (11:19).

decisions.choice: give rest: refresh, give relief
decisions.reason: The verb means to let someone stop and recover.

records.heading: Come to me and find rest

records.source: ἄρατε τὸν ζυγόν μου ἐφ’ ὑμᾶς καὶ μάθετε ἀπ’ ἐμοῦ, ὅτι πραΰς εἰμι καὶ ταπεινὸς τῇ καρδίᾳ, καὶ εὑρήσετε ἀνάπαυσιν ταῖς ψυχαῖς ὑμῶν·
records.gloss: Take the yoke of me upon you and learn from me, for gentle I am and humble in the heart, and you will find rest for the souls of you;
pieces: Put {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} yoke on your necks and learn from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, because I am gentle and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} heart is humble. Then you will find rest for your souls.

L.29: Take {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} yoke upon you and learn from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, for I am gentle and humble in heart, and you will find rest for your souls.

R.29: Take {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} yoke and put it on, and learn from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. I am gentle and humble. And you will find rest for your souls.

decisions.choice: yoke: the wooden bar that joins working animals at the neck; a picture of teaching that one takes on
decisions.reason: A yoke let animals pull a load. Jewish teachers spoke of taking on the yoke of the law or of the kingdom, and Sirach 51:26 of wisdom's yoke. To take Jesus's yoke is to follow his teaching.

decisions.choice: you will find rest for your souls: Jeremiah 6:16
decisions.reason: God tells Israel to walk in the good, ancient way, and they will find rest for their souls. Israel refused; Jesus offers that rest.

decisions.choice: gentle and humble in heart: meek and lowly, not harsh or proud
decisions.reason: "Gentle" is the word of 5:5 and 21:5. "Humble" means lowly; Jesus is a teacher unlike those who load others down (23:4).

decisions.choice: learn from me: become my disciple
decisions.reason: The verb is related to the word for disciple, one who learns.

decisions.choice: on your necks
decisions.reason: Balanced shows where a yoke is worn.

records.source: ὁ γὰρ ζυγός μου χρηστὸς καὶ τὸ φορτίον μου ἐλαφρόν ἐστιν.
records.gloss: The for yoke of me kind and the burden of me light is.
pieces: For {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} yoke is easy to wear, and the load I give is light."

L.30: For {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} yoke [is] easy, and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} burden is light."

R.30: The yoke I give you is easy to wear. The load I ask you to carry is light."

decisions.choice: easy: kind, good, fitting well
decisions.reason: The word means good or kind. Of a yoke it means one that fits well and does not rub. Jesus still calls people to obey (5:19-20).

decisions.choice: burden: the load Jesus asks his followers to carry
decisions.reason: The noun matches the verb "burdened" in 11:28, and contrasts with the heavy loads of 23:4.

decisions.choice: easy (L); easy to wear (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Kind yoke" is not natural English. "Easy to wear" keeps the picture of the yoke.
